plan.contextChunk: This figure contains five panels (a)–(e) tracing the execution of the Bellman-Ford algorithm on a directed weighted graph with five vertices s, t, x, y, and z and ten directed edges with weights 6, 7, 5, 8, −4, −2, −3, 9, 7, and 2. The same graph layout is used in all five panels: vertex s appears at the left, t and y in the center-left region, and x and z at the right; each vertex circle displays the current shortest-path estimate d[v] inside it. Panel (a) shows the initial state with d[s] = 0 and d[v] = ∞ for all other vertices, and all edges drawn as thin black arrows labeled with their weights. Panels (b) through (e) each show the graph after one additional relaxation pass; bold gray arrows highlight the edges whose relaxation improved a distance estimate in that pass, and updated d[v] values appear inside the affected vertex circles. After pass 1 (panel b), d[t] = 6 and d[y] = 7. After pass 2 (panel c), d[x] = 4 and d[z] = 2. After pass 3 (panel d), d[t] = 2 and d[z] = −2. Panel (e) shows the final shortest-path estimates d[s] = 0, d[t] = 2, d[x] = 4, d[y] = 7, d[z] = −2, with bold arrows forming the shortest-path tree along the path s → y → x → t → z. This figure demonstrates the Bellman-Ford algorithm's iterative relaxation process, showing how negative-weight edges cause distance estimates to decrease over successive passes until convergence.

demo_steps.title: Textbook overview
demo_steps.narration: The default view shows all five panels in the original three-over-two arrangement, with only the source captions '(a)' through '(e)' inside the figure area.

demo_steps.title: Initial estimates
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a) starts Bellman-Ford with d[s]=0 and every other vertex at infinity because no path has been discovered yet.

demo_steps.title: After the first pass
demo_steps.narration: Panel (b) shows that the source has reached t and y, so the predecessor highlights begin with edges s -> t and s -> y.

demo_steps.title: After the second pass
demo_steps.narration: Panel (c) shows improved estimates propagating farther: y improves x to 4, and t reaches z with estimate 2.

demo_steps.title: After the third pass
demo_steps.narration: Panel (d) shows the negative edge x -> t lowering d[t] from 6 to 2, replacing t's predecessor with x.

demo_steps.title: After the fourth pass
demo_steps.narration: Panel (e) shows the improved value of t propagating through t -> z, giving the final shortest-path tree s -> y -> x -> t -> z.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Each full Bellman-Ford pass lets better distance information move one edge farther, so the shortest-path tree emerges gradually rather than all at once.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Default rendering must be a faithful multipanel textbook replacement: show all five panels at once in a 3-over-2 grid, with captions exactly '(a)', '(b)', '(c)', '(d)', and '(e)' inside the figure area and no explanatory sentences, pass counters, change counters, candidate-distance callouts, or calculation annotations in the figure. Use the same compact graph layout in each panel: s left, t above y in the middle, x above z on the right. Vertices should be light gray circles with black outlines, vertex names near the circles, and distance estimates centered inside. Draw all directed edges as thin black arrows with black arrowheads and weight labels. Draw highlighted predecessor edges as broad semi-transparent gray bands underneath the corresponding black edges; do not draw separate gray arrowheads. The black edge strokes and black arrowheads should remain visible on top of the gray bands. In guided single-panel mode, show only the selected panel enlarged, still preserving the exact source caption and the same no-callout styling; put all explanatory text in the UI narration panel only.

plan.concept: Bellman-Ford finds shortest paths by repeatedly relaxing every edge, allowing negative-weight edges to lower distance estimates over several passes until no better estimates remain.

interactions.label: Implement Bellman-Ford relaxation

api.does: return the current shortest-path estimate d[v] for vertex v
true when numeric value a is smaller than numeric value b, including comparisons with Infinity
update d[v] to value and record a frame showing the new number inside vertex v
set u as the predecessor of v and redraw the current predecessor-tree highlight
highlight the directed edge u -> v for the current frame with a short note such as 'relaxed' or 'no change'

interactions.frame: Each recorded frame shows the whole graph, the currently inspected edge, the candidate value d[u] + w, all current distance labels inside the vertices, the current predecessor-tree edges in bold gray, and the pass/change counters.

input.label: Fixed Bellman-Ford edge order and initial distances
input.default: dist.s = 0; dist.t = dist.x = dist.y = dist.z = Infinity; edges repeated for 4 passes: t->x:5, t->y:8, t->z:-4, x->t:-2, y->x:-3, y->z:9, z->x:7, z->s:2, s->t:6, s->y:7

interactions.success_check: After four full passes, the final estimates are d[s]=0, d[t]=2, d[x]=4, d[y]=7, d[z]=-2, and the predecessor edges form the shortest-path tree s -> y -> x -> t -> z.
interactions.teaches: A relaxation step only changes a vertex when the route through the current edge is cheaper, and repeated passes let improvements propagate across paths with multiple edges, including negative-weight edges.

demo_steps.title: Initialize estimates
demo_steps.narration: Only the source s starts with distance 0; every other vertex is marked infinity because no path has been discovered yet.

demo_steps.title: Pass 1: leave the source
demo_steps.narration: The first useful relaxations come from s, setting d[t]=6 and d[y]=7. The gray edges show the first discovered paths outward from the source.

demo_steps.title: Pass 2: propagate one edge farther
demo_steps.narration: Now that t and y are reachable, their outgoing edges can improve other vertices: x becomes 4 through y, and z becomes 2 through t.

demo_steps.title: Pass 3: a negative edge improves t
demo_steps.narration: The edge x -> t has weight -2, so the route s -> y -> x -> t lowers d[t] from 6 to 2 even though t was already reachable.

demo_steps.title: Pass 4: final improvement reaches z
demo_steps.narration: The improved value of t propagates through t -> z, lowering d[z] to -2. The final predecessor chain is s -> y -> x -> t -> z.

plan.keyInsight: Bellman-Ford works because each pass lets shorter information travel one more edge along a path, so negative edges can still be handled as long as repeated relaxation eventually stabilizes.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Use a grayscale CLRS-style network diagram: light gray circular vertices with black outlines, italic vertex names just outside the circles, and the current d[v] value centered inside each circle using ∞ for infinity. Arrange s at far left, t above y in the middle-left, and x above z at the right. Draw all arrows thin and black with clear weight labels; use curved opposing arrows between t and x so weights 5 and -2 are visually distinct. During replay, overlay thick semi-transparent gray arrows on relaxed or predecessor edges without hiding the black arrowheads or weight labels. The final emphasized tree should read visually as s -> y -> x -> t -> z, with distance labels 0, 7, 4, 2, and -2 respectively.

plan.reconstructionNotes: Default rendering must be a faithful multipanel textbook replacement: show all five panels at once in a 3-over-2 grid, with captions exactly '(a)', '(b)', '(c)', '(d)', and '(e)' inside the figure area and no explanatory sentences, pass counters, change counters, candidate-distance callouts, or calculation annotations in the figure. Use the same compact graph layout in each panel: s left, t above y in the middle, x above z on the right. Vertices should be light gray circles with black outlines, vertex names near the circles, and distance estimates centered inside. Draw all directed edges as thin black arrows with black arrowheads and weight labels. Draw highlighted predecessor edges as broad semi-transparent gray bands underneath the corresponding black edges; do not draw separate gray arrowheads. The black edge strokes and black arrowheads should remain visible on top of the gray bands. In guided single-panel mode, show only the selected panel enlarged, still preserving the exact source caption and the same no-callout styling; put all explanatory text in the UI narration panel only.
